subject: general
question: What is the name of the Super Expressway that links the metropolitan cities of New Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Golden Quadrilateral**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Golden Quadrilateral** is a network of highways in India connecting the four major metropolitan cities: **New Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata**.
 
• It is one of the largest highway projects in India and was initiated by the **Government of India under the National Highways Development Project (NHDP)**.
 
• The project was launched in **2001** and was completed in phases, aiming to improve connectivity between major cities and promote economic development.
 
• The **Golden Quadrilateral** spans a length of approximately **5,846 kilometers**, covering major industrial and agricultural centers of India.
 
• This expressway facilitates rapid transportation of goods and passengers, significantly reducing travel time and fuel consumption.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Features of the Golden Quadrilateral:**

 
 
• The expressway is designed to meet **international standards** of road infrastructure.
 
• It connects cities with high economic and industrial significance, boosting **trade and commerce** across the nation.
 
• The road infrastructure includes **multiple lanes, bypasses, flyovers, and service roads** to ensure smooth traffic flow and reduce congestion.
 
 
 
• **Importance:**
 
 
• The Golden Quadrilateral plays a vital role in reducing travel time and improving connectivity between India's major cities.
 
• It facilitates **economic growth** by enabling faster transportation of goods and services.
 
• Improved road infrastructure has led to a rise in **tourism, industrial development, and urbanization**.
 
 
 
• **Other Related Projects:**
 
 
• The **North-South and East-West Corridor** connects Srinagar to Kanyakumari and Silchar to Porbandar, respectively.
 
• **National Highway 44** is India's longest highway, connecting Srinagar to Kanyakumari, but it is not part of the Golden Quadrilateral.
 
• The **East-West Corridor** is another major infrastructure project aimed at improving connectivity across India.
 
 
 
• **Facts and Figures:**
 
 
• The Golden Quadrilateral was built at a cost of approximately **Rs. 60,000 crore**.
 
• It includes **four-lane and six-lane roads** with advanced features like electronic toll collection systems.
 
• The project is maintained by the **National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)**.
